candidates.why: Line 752 does a shallow copy `Bit_Chain dat1 = *hdl_dat`, so dat1.chain aliases the original _hdl_dat.chain. bit_chain_free(&dat1) at 759 frees that chain, but the original _hdl_dat (and any other alias of the same chain pointer) is left dangling; the subsequent `*hdl_dat = *dat` at 761 only overwrites dat2, not _hdl_dat, so _hdl_dat.chain remains a freed pointer.

hdl_dat was set to &dat2 at 755; bit_chain_free(&dat2) at 760 frees dat2.chain, then line 761 `*hdl_dat = *dat` writes over dat2 (hdl_dat==&dat2). The freed chain pointer is overwritten (leak), and any alias of dat2.chain taken earlier would be a use-after-free.

In the encrypted branch, free(sec_dat[type].chain) at 3113 frees the section buffer; it is reassigned at 3114, but `dat` may still alias &sec_dat[type] (set at 3004/2936) and sec_dat[type].chain is read again at 3121/3129. If the reassignment path is skipped or dat aliases the old chain, this is a use-after-free.

bit_chain_free(&sec_dat[type]) at 3133 frees each section chain in the loop; `dat` was reset to old_dat at 3039 so normally safe, but if any earlier assignment left dat aliasing &sec_dat[type] (e.g. 3004/2936), the later use of dat->chain at 3166/3170 would touch freed memory.
